podcast.title: Songwriter of "What A Wonderful World" (1967)
podcast.body: George David Weiss was the songwriter who, along with producer Bob Thiele, offered the orchestral pop ballad "What A Wonderful World" to Louis Armstrong in 1967. "Three years later, Armstrong was offered an orchestral pop ballad about the wonders of existence by producer Bob Feel and songwriter George David Weiss."

podcast.title: Advocate for Intellectual Property
podcast.body: According to his obituary in The Guardian, George Weiss was a familiar figure at congressional hearings advocating for copyright reform and protection against music piracy, emphasizing the vital importance of intellectual property for composers. "According to George Weiss' obituary in the Guardian, he was a familiar figure at congressional hearings into copyright reform and music piracy, testifying as to the vital importance of intellectual property protection for composers."

podcast.title: Copyright Renewal Dispute with Richmond Organization
podcast.body: In 1989, when the 28-year copyright term for "The Lion Sleeps Tonight" expired, George Weiss filed to renew the copyright and intended to prevent the Richmond Organization from publishing the song. This led to a court battle where Weiss successfully argued that the Richmond Organization had acknowledged him as a writer since 1961. "George Weiss filed notice that he was going to renew the copyright when the 28 year term expired, and that he wasn't going to let the Richmond Organization publish the song."

podcast.title: Influential Figure in the Industry
podcast.body: Weiss was described as someone with a lot of influence in the music industry, which contributed to an "amicable agreement" that allowed him and Hugo and Luigi to retain songwriting credit and royalties for "The Lion Sleeps Tonight." "Wiss was someone who had a lot of influence in the industry and who nobody wanted to upset, and so they came to a very amicable agreement."

podcast.title: Inquiry into Original "In Boube" Meaning
podcast.body: Weiss decided to investigate the original lyrics of "In Boube" (Wimoweh), and reportedly consulted the South African consulate, who confirmed it was about lions. This informed his new English lyrics for "The Lion Sleeps Tonight." "Wiss decided to find out what the original lyrics have been about, and apparently asked the South African consulate, who told him that it was about Lions."

podcast.title: Professional Writer for Hugo and Luigi
podcast.body: George David Weiss was a professional writer with whom the production duo Hugo and Luigi had worked before, notably on "Can't Help Falling in Love" for Elvis Presley. "They decided to get a professional writer in to fix the song-up, and called in George David Weiss, a writer with whom they'd worked before."
